findings.title: Delete menu item never renders in the list view
findings.body: The Delete menu is gated by `canDelete && rulerRule && (...)`. In the list view the consumer (`GrafanaRuleListItem`/`RuleActionsButtons.V2`) only passes `promRule`, so `rulerRule` is `undefined`. The new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` evaluates `canDelete` to `true` for users with delete permission on Grafana folders, but the render guard short-circuits to `false` and the Delete option is hidden anyway. Effectively users will not be able to delete Grafana-managed rules from the list view even though the abilities hook reports they can.

findings.title: Pause menu item never renders in the list view
findings.body: The Pause menu item is gated by `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana'`. In the list view `rulerRule` is `undefined`, so `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(undefined)` returns `false` and the Pause option is hidden even though `canPause` (computed via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) may be true. Users lose the ability to pause Grafana-managed rules from the list view.

findings.title: Silence action does nothing in the list view
findings.body: When the user clicks Silence, `handleSilence` sets `showSilenceDrawer=true`. The drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, but `rule` is `undefined` in the list view. So `showSilenceDrawer` flips to `true` and nothing visible happens. The grafana-only `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` was never made to accept `promRule`, so silence is silently broken for the list view, despite `canSilence` evaluating `true` via the new abilities.

findings.title: Missing React key prop on <GrafanaRuleListItem>
findings.body: When migrating from `GrafanaRuleLoader` to `GrafanaRuleListItem`, the `key={key}` prop was dropped from the Grafana branch of the list switch (the datasource branch still passes `key={key}`). React will warn about missing keys in the filtered list and, more importantly, component state (e.g. menu open/close, hook subscriptions) will not be preserved correctly across reorders and unmounts because React falls back to using array index.

findings.title: Creating and Deleting transient states no longer rendered
findings.body: The previous version fetched both Prometheus and Ruler groups and used `matchRules` to distinguish three cases: rules present in both (normal), rules only in ruler (rendered with `RuleOperation.Creating`), and rules only in Prometheus (rendered with `RuleOperation.Deleting`). This PR removes the Ruler fetch and the entire matching logic, so rules that are in the middle of being created/deleted will silently appear as ordinary active rules, with no Creating/Deleting badge. The `operation={RuleOperation.Creating}` and `RuleOperationListItem` props are still accepted by `GrafanaRuleListItem` but nothing ever computes them now.

findings.title: Tests for Creating/Deleting transient state were deleted
findings.body: The original `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` covered `should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists` and `should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists`, plus three unit tests for `matchRules`. All have been removed in this PR. Since the deletion of those behaviors is a regression risk (see the previous finding), these tests should be retained (or replaced with new tests asserting the new equivalent behavior) to prevent re-introducing the bug.

findings.title: Stale `// duplicate` comment in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities
findings.body: Line 289 in `useAbilities.ts` reads: `const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate`. The trailing `// duplicate` looks like a leftover TODO/scratchpad marker. It is meaningless to future readers and should be removed or replaced with an explanatory comment.

findings.title: Redundant triple mock reset in beforeEach
findings.body: The `beforeEach` block calls `jest.clearAllMocks(); jest.restoreAllMocks(); jest.resetAllMocks();` sequentially. Calling all three is redundant (each fully resets call/spy state) and can mask the intent of which reset is actually needed. Pick the single appropriate call. Also, because the mocks are then re-set up immediately with default returns, the order/selection matters: if `clearAllMocks` is removed, the previously installed `mockImplementation` from the previous test would persist for unwired mocks, potentially producing subtle cross-test contamination.
